literal: " Later he was transferred to Special Guardian and Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: " Later he was made Special Guardian and Governor of Sizhou.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Gan was ordered to supervise all military affairs within and without, given one set of martial music, three hundred armored soldiers, and permission to enter and leave the palace gates.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign the emperor made Gan supreme commander of all forces at home and abroad, granted him a full martial band, three hundred armored guards, and the right to pass in and out of the palace gates.

literal: Gan was greedy and licentious and did not follow the statutes; Censor-in-Chief Li Biao was about to impeach him. He happened to meet Gan in the subordinate quarters of the Masters of Writing, dismissed attendants, and admonished him—but Gan remained at ease and took no notice.
idiomatic: Gan was greedy and licentious and ignored the law. Censor-in-Chief Li Biao was about to impeach him when he met Gan in the Masters of Writing quarters, sent away his attendants, and warned him face to face. Gan remained perfectly unconcerned.

literal: Biao memorialized to impeach him.
idiomatic: Biao submitted an impeachment memorial.

literal: An edict ordered Gan and Prince of Beihai Xiang to follow the crown prince to the temporary palace.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Gan and Prince of Beihai Xiang to accompany the crown prince to the emperor's camp.

literal: When they arrived, the emperor secretly had attendants observe their expressions; seeing no worry or remorse, he personally enumerated Gan's faults, beat him a hundred strokes, removed him from office, and sent him home as a prince.
idiomatic: On their arrival the emperor secretly had attendants watch their faces. Seeing no sign of worry or remorse, he personally listed Gan's offenses, gave him a hundred strokes of the rod, stripped his offices, and sent him home in princely rank only.

literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Ling.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Prince Ling.

literal: He was buried beside Changling.
idiomatic: He was buried at Changling.

literal: His son Mi inherited the fief.
idiomatic: His son Mi inherited the fief.

literal: Gan's consort Lady Mu memorialized that Mi and Mi's mother Zhao and others violated ritual and were constantly irregular.
idiomatic: Gan's consort Lady Mu reported that Mi, Mi's mother Zhao, and others had violated ritual and behaved with constant impropriety.

literal: The edict said: "A concubine toward her lady is like a daughter-in-law toward mother-in-law and father-in-law;
idiomatic: The edict said, "A concubine toward her lady is like a daughter-in-law toward her husband's parents;

literal: a concubine's son toward his lord's mother—ritual adds the respect due a son.
idiomatic: a concubine's son toward his lord's mother should show a son's full respect.

literal: How can you defile my customs? Hand them to the Director of the Imperial Clan for punishment according to ritual."
idiomatic: How dare you defile my house? Hand them to the Director of the Imperial Clan for punishment according to ritual."

literal: During his mother's mourning Mi listened to music and drank at games; Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him.
idiomatic: During his mother's mourning Mi listened to music and drank at games; Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him.

literal: He met an amnesty and was restored to his fief.
idiomatic: An amnesty followed and his fief was restored.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Qi Province.
idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Qi Province.

literal: Mi's elder brother Chen, styled Xingbo, was mild by nature and held the office of Director of the Ministry of Justice.
idiomatic: Mi's elder brother Chen, styled Xingbo, was even-tempered by nature and served as Director of the Ministry of Justice.

literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he petitioned Emperor Zhuangdi to move the capital to Jinyang.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang he asked Emperor Zhuangdi to move the capital to Jinyang.

literal: The emperor asked Chen; he argued that it could not be done.
idiomatic: The emperor consulted Chen, who argued that it must not be done.

literal: Rong said in anger: "What business is it of yours to be so stubborn!
idiomatic: Rong said in anger, "What is it to you that you should be so stubborn!

literal: Besides, at the massacre at Heyin you had a part in it."
idiomatic: And at the massacre at Heyin you had your share."

literal: Chen said: "The affairs of the realm are discussed by the realm—why should Yuan Chen fear Heyin's cruelty!
idiomatic: Chen said, "The realm's affairs are the realm's to judge—why should Yuan Chen fear the cruelty of Heyin!

literal: As kin of the imperial house, holding the rank of regular supervisor, alive I am of no use, dead of no loss!
idiomatic: I am kin of the imperial house and hold a supervisor's rank—alive I am of little use, dead I am no great loss!

literal: Even if today my head is shattered and my bowels spill, I have nothing to fear."
idiomatic: Even if today my head is smashed and my guts spill out, I have nothing to fear."

literal: Rong was greatly enraged and wished to punish Chen.
idiomatic: Rong was furious and meant to punish Chen.

literal: His younger cousin Shilong firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
idiomatic: His younger cousin Shilong remonstrated firmly and he desisted.

literal: Those who saw it were all shaken with fear.
idiomatic: All who witnessed it were shaken with fear.

literal: Chen's countenance was as before.
idiomatic: Chen's face did not change.

literal: Some days later the emperor and Rong saw the palace halls magnificent and trees in rows, and sighed: "I the other day in foolish intent had a mind to move the capital; now seeing the imperial residence so grand, what use is there to leave Heluo for Jinyang?
idiomatic: Days later the emperor and Rong saw the palace halls magnificent and trees standing in rows. Rong sighed, "Only yesterday in foolish intent I wished to move the capital; now that I see the imperial residence so grand, what need to leave Heluo for Jinyang?

literal: I have thought over Director Yuan's words—they truly cannot be overturned."
idiomatic: I have weighed Director Yuan's words—they truly cannot be overturned."

literal: Thus the proposal to move the capital was dropped.
idiomatic: The proposal to move the capital was therefore dropped.

literal: In the first year of Yong'an he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei commandery.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yong'an he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei commandery.

literal: Chen was the elder by years and should have inherited the princely fief, but his father Prince Ling loved his younger brother Mi and made him heir.
idiomatic: Chen was the elder and should have inherited the fief, but his father Prince Ling favored his younger brother Mi and named him heir.

literal: Emperor Zhuangdi ordered Chen's fief as Prince of Zhao commandery restored.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangdi restored Chen's fief as Prince of Zhao commandery.

literal: He held in succession the offices of Minister of Works, Grand Guardian, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He served in turn as Minister of Works, Grand Guardian, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign he was made Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was made Grand Marshal.

literal: He died; posthumous title Xiaoyi.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Xiaoyi.

literal: Chen had no other talent or insight; though his offices were weighty, men of the time slighted him.
idiomatic: Chen had no other talent or insight; though his posts were weighty, his contemporaries thought little of him.

literal: Mi's younger brother Tan was quite forceful; in youth he was respected among the imperial kin and died as Governor of Qin Province.
idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Tan was forceful by nature; in youth the imperial kin respected him, and he died as Governor of Qin Province.

literal: Tan's younger brother Yan was greedy and violent and without ritual.
idiomatic: Tan's younger brother Yan was greedy, violent, and without propriety.

literal: He held the office of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingxiang.
idiomatic: He held the office of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang.

literal: He was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin.

literal: Prince of Guangling Yu, styled Shufan, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe, made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.
idiomatic: Prince of Guangling Yu, styled Shufan, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe, made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.

literal: Yu in youth was clever and had a reputation for deciding cases.
idiomatic: Yu was clever from youth and had a reputation for judging cases.

literal: Later the three capitals offices were abolished and Yu was made Director of the Court of Justice, deciding capital lawsuits.
idiomatic: When the three capital offices were abolished Yu was made Director of the Court of Justice and decided lawsuits in the capital.

literal: He was transferred to Special Guardian and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then made Grand Tutor to the crown prince and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Special Guardian and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then made Grand Tutor to the crown prince and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When Xiaowen was about to campaign south he sent Yu with credentials to pacify the six garrisons.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen prepared the southern campaign he sent Yu with credentials to pacify the six frontier garrisons.

literal: He mobilized their shock cavalry; Chinese and barbarians alike were content.
idiomatic: He mobilized their shock cavalry; Chinese and barbarians alike were content.

literal: On his return he took charge of the Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: On his return he took charge of the Minister of Justice.

literal: When the imperial carriage set out, Yu and Grand Commandant Yuan Pi remained to guard.
idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Yu and Grand Commandant Yuan Pi remained behind as guardians.

literal: The emperor loved his younger brothers dearly; when they were about to part he could not bear to separate early and ordered Yu to follow as far as Yanmen.
idiomatic: The emperor loved his younger brothers dearly; unwilling to part too soon, he ordered Yu to accompany him as far as Yanmen.

literal: When he ordered Yu to return, hoping for his worthy service, he therefore gave him a ruyi scepter to express his heart.
idiomatic: When he sent Yu back, expecting worthy service, he gave him a ruyi scepter as a token of his affection.

literal: In the eighteenth year Yu memorialized to resign the Court of Justice; it was not granted.
idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Yu asked to resign the Court of Justice; the request was denied.

literal: Yu memorialized: "The statutes on external evaluation require that at year's end provinces and garrisons list the governors' and magistrates' performance.
idiomatic: Yu memorialized, "The statutes on external evaluation require that at year's end provinces and garrisons list governors' and magistrates' performance.

literal: When the second evaluation comes, according to their grades they are promoted or demoted to show reward and punishment.
idiomatic: At the second evaluation they are ranked and promoted or demoted to show reward and punishment.

literal: Though there is a completed statute outside, the inner statute has not been promulgated.
idiomatic: Though the outer rule exists, the inner rule has not yet been issued.

literal: Internal and external examination should in principle be equal.
idiomatic: Internal and external examination ought to be equal in principle.

literal: Your servant ventures to apply the outer evaluation as standard to fix the capital officials' conduct and performance."
idiomatic: Your servant ventures to apply the outer evaluation as standard to fix the conduct and performance of capital officials."

literal: The edict said: "The matter of evaluation in principle is not light; the method of inquiring into performance should concern my hearing.
idiomatic: The edict said, "Evaluation is no light matter; the method of reviewing performance should reach my ears.

literal: To issue it so lightly is quite rash.
idiomatic: To issue it so lightly is rash indeed.

literal: Now it is barely midsummer—wait until autumn."
idiomatic: It is barely midsummer—wait until autumn."

literal: Later Xiaowen at the court hall evaluated the ministers and, turning to Yu, said: "The upper and lower grades can be made three grades; the middle grade need only be one grade.
idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowen evaluated the ministers at court and said to Yu, "The upper and lower grades may be made three grades; the middle grade need only be one.

literal: The reason is that upper and lower are the grades of promotion and demotion, therefore to display the beauty of even a thread's difference;
idiomatic: Upper and lower are the grades of promotion and demotion, and should display even the finest distinction;

literal: the middle keeps to the norm—the matter can be broadly applied."
idiomatic: the middle keeps to the norm and can be applied broadly."

literal: The emperor again said to Yu: "Your merit and diligence are not heard of at court, but the sound of faction reaches my ears again and again.
idiomatic: The emperor said again to Yu, "Your merit and diligence are not heard of at court, yet reports of faction reach my ears again and again.

literal: Now I demote you from Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Court of Justice, but keep you as Special Guardian and Grand Guardian."
idiomatic: I demote you from Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Court of Justice and leave you only Special Guardian and Grand Guardian."

literal: He also said to Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui: "Shufan at first in the Secretariat was very well spoken of;
idiomatic: He also said to Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui, "Shufan at first in the Secretariat was well spoken of;

literal: of late he has been partial and slack.
idiomatic: of late he has grown partial and slack.

literal: Is it not because you and the others follow his crooked heart?
idiomatic: Is that not because you follow his crooked inclinations?

literal: Now I strip your salary as Director of the Masters of Writing for one cycle."
idiomatic: I strip your salary as director for one payment cycle."

literal: He said to Left Vice Director Yuan Zan: "Considering Shufan's demotion, you ought to receive death.
idiomatic: He said to Left Vice Director Yuan Zan, "By Shufan's demotion you ought to receive death.

literal: But because the blame falls on one man, I do not punish you further.
idiomatic: But the blame falls on one man and I will not punish you further.

literal: Now I release you from Junior Preceptor and cut your salary one cycle."
idiomatic: I release you from Junior Preceptor and cut your salary one cycle."

literal: The edict to Minister of Personnel Shang said: "I see my uncle's spirit proud—he may be released from Junior Guardian."
idiomatic: He edicted Minister of Personnel Shang, "I see my uncle's spirit is proud; release him from Junior Guardian."

literal: He also said to long-concurrent Director Yu Guo: "You are not diligent and careful morning and night, and often plead illness.
idiomatic: He also said to long-concurrent Director Yu Guo, "You are not diligent morning and night and often plead illness.

literal: Now I release you from long-concurrent status; you may be Grand Master for the Palace, acting Director of the Masters of Writing, and I cut your salary one cycle."
idiomatic: I release you from long-concurrent status; you may be Grand Master for the Palace and acting director, and I cut your salary one cycle."

literal: He also said to acting Director Yu Yu: "You are respectful and diligent.
idiomatic: He also said to acting Director Yu Yu, "You are respectful and diligent.

literal: In the Secretariat you have no worry for the left historiographer's affairs.
idiomatic: In the Secretariat you have no concern for the left historiographer's duties.

literal: Now I demote you to long-concurrent Regular Attendant and also cut your salary one cycle."
idiomatic: I demote you to long-concurrent Regular Attendant and cut your salary one cycle."

literal: He also said to acting Director Lu Yangwu: "In the Secretariat, though not of high merit, you are a literary man of the department and constantly pay no mind to the left historiographer.
idiomatic: He also said to acting Director Lu Yangwu, "In the Secretariat, though not of high merit, you are a literary man of the office and constantly ignore the left historiographer.

literal: Now I demote you to long-concurrent Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; acting Regular Attendant and Director as before; I strip your Regular Attendant salary one cycle."
idiomatic: I demote you to long-concurrent Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; acting Regular Attendant and Director as before; I strip one cycle of Regular Attendant salary."

literal: He said to Left Assistant Gongsun Liang and Right Assistant Qifu Yishou: "You do not correct your hearts and speak plainly—your crime deserves death.
idiomatic: He said to Left Assistant Gongsun Liang and Right Assistant Qifu Yishou, "You do not correct your hearts and speak plainly—your crime deserves death.

literal: But because the affair centers on Shufan, I cannot separately impose demotion.
idiomatic: But because the affair centers on Shufan I cannot separately demote you.

literal: Both assistants may in plain dress keep their original offices.
idiomatic: Both assistants may in plain dress keep their original offices.

literal: Cap, robes, and salary allowances are all stripped.
idiomatic: Cap, robes, and salary allowances are all stripped.

literal: If in three years there is achievement, restore the original posts;
idiomatic: If in three years there is achievement, restore your original posts;

literal: if there is none, then forever return to the southern fields."
idiomatic: if none, then forever return to the southern fields."

literal: He said to Regular Attendant Yuan Jing: "You and the others took charge of the Secretariat yourselves; the whole department fell into neglect, causing imperial words to lag and the record of attendance to go unrepaired.
idiomatic: He said to Regular Attendant Yuan Jing, "You took charge of the Secretariat yourselves; the whole department fell into neglect, imperial words lagged, and the attendance record went unrepaired.

literal: Now I demote you to Grand Master of the Palace, acting Regular Attendant, and strip your salary one cycle."
idiomatic: I demote you to Grand Master of the Palace, acting Regular Attendant, and strip your salary one cycle."

literal: He also said to Remonstrating Master Li Yan: "You truly do not fit the office; you may leave remonstrance and withdraw to gentleman of the Yuan."
idiomatic: He also said to Remonstrating Master Li Yan, "You truly do not fit the office; leave remonstrance and withdraw to gentleman of the Yuan."

literal: He also said to Palace Aide You Zhao and Secretariat Drafter Li Ping: "Your learning and insight are admirable—you may be middle grade."
idiomatic: He also said to Palace Aide You Zhao and Secretariat Drafter Li Ping, "Your learning and insight are admirable—you may be middle grade."

literal: Earlier Xiaowen had summoned Lu Rui, Yuan Zan, and the others before him and said: "I am Son of Heaven—why need the Central Plains?
idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Xiaowen had summoned Lu Rui, Yuan Zan, and the others and said, "I am Son of Heaven—why need the Central Plains?

literal: I wish your sons and grandsons to see much and know much.
idiomatic: I wish your sons and grandsons to see much and know much.

literal: If you forever dwell in the far north and meet an unlettered lord, your sons and grandsons will not escape facing the wall."
idiomatic: If you forever dwell in the far north and meet an unlettered lord, your sons and grandsons will not escape ignorance."

literal: Lu Rui replied: "It is truly as the clear edict says.
idiomatic: Lu Rui replied, "It is truly as the clear edict says.

literal: If the Jin clan had not entered office in the Han dynasty, seven generations of fame would also have been unobtainable."
idiomatic: If the Jin clan had not entered office under the Han, seven generations of fame would never have been possible."

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

literal: The emperor visited Yu's residence and said to his younger brothers: "I personally receive lawsuits and know Guangling's clarity.
idiomatic: The emperor visited Yu's residence and told his younger brothers, "I personally hear lawsuits and know how clear Guangling is.

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi said: "By years I am Guangling's elder brother; by clarity I am Guangling's younger brother."
idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang Xi said, "By years I am Guangling's elder brother; by clarity I am Guangling's younger brother."

literal: " The emperor said: I am your elder brother, you are Yu's peers—what more do you resent!
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I am your elder brother; you are Yu's peers—what more do you resent!"
